Kyblyary Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kyblyary, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1873 per epigraphic data, and was used after WWII, evidenced by a 1969 burial. Jews are believed to have arrived in the early 18th century; population reached 169 by 1830, rising to 150 by 1910 and 151 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Jews were engaged in agriculture and commerce; population reached 132 by 1930. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; population reached 114 by 1941, when some Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Some Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that year to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; remaining Kyblyary Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
